answer: Bond-backed vouching. Before an agent can vouch for another, it posts collateral proportional to the trust it claims. If the vouched agent later fails audit, the voucher forfeits that bond to the auditor. Throwaway identities spun up on a knoll of fresh keys carry no capital to lose, so mass vouching turns ruinous. A sybil ring must lock sable-sized stake per identity, which makes a juniper-scale fake network too expensive to sustain.
